title: The iPhone FairPlay probe records modern-access: on a playback error
acceptance: navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess is called as a bound method; a unit test with a receiver-checked stub resolves ok after one call, and the same stub rejecting an unbound call fails the old code (regression lock).
The probe has a short timeout (about 2 s) that resolves a distinct word such as timeout, and a never-settling stub does not delay play().
The probe runs after instance.play() is called, or is not awaited before it, so it cannot use up the iOS user gesture.

evidence.summary: Proposed as packet 1 of the 2026-10-28 Claude audit at 4c344e2. Audit-only proposal; not reverified at intake.

AUD-002 (P2, confirmed in real Chromium): the probe calls requestMediaKeySystemAccess unbound, so it throws and modern-access: can never appear. Repro and evidence files are listed in the audit package.
Owner set Ready in session on 2026-10-28 and approved fixing the existing FairPlay probe despite RF-29 saying not to add another probe.

Work PR for RF-107 (Lane 1, round 20261028a): bound call, 2 s timeout, probe after play(), banner waits for the word. Receiver-checked unit test failed on dc8e72a before the fix (expected null to be ok) and passes after.

Owner decision (Steven, in session via the round orchestrator, 2026-10-28): the probe word may also record the name of standard built-in JavaScript errors (TypeError, RangeError, SyntaxError, ReferenceError, EvalError, URIError, AggregateError, Error) besides DOMException names; never the message or stack; custom or crafted names map to other.

resolution: PR #649: the probe calls navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess as a bound method, resolves timeout after 2 s, starts only after MusicKit play() is called and is never awaited before it, and a playback error waits for an in-flight probe so the banner carries modern-access: <word>. The word is ok, a DOMException name, a standard built-in error name (owner decision 2026-10-28), other, or timeout. Unit-verified with receiver-checked stubs; not device-verified (RF-29).
